title: Existence of the degree-zero tower witness for a normalized diagonal source
statement: theorem diagonalTrace_limitWitness_exists (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian (ProjectiveLine Y)] [IsNoetherian (diagonalSurface Y)] (hY : IsUnit (l : Γ(Y, ⊤))) [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l Y] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (ProjectiveLine Y)] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l (diagonalSurface Y)] (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction l (diagonalScalarExtension l (diagonalSurface Y))) (δ : diagonalCompletedDomain l Y ⟶ diagonalCompletedCodomain l Y) (hδ : IsDiagonalLimit l Y hY D δ) (f : diagonalSurface Y ⟶ ProjectiveLine Y) (hf : f = pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) ∨ f = pullback.snd (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)) (t : Result l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) f) (a : SupportedSource l Y f t.Rc) : ∃ s : SingleTowerLimitWitness (DiagonalMod l (ProjectiveLine Y)) ((diagonalCompletedUnderlying l (ProjectiveLine Y)).map (a.hom ≫ t.Rc.R.map δ ≫ t.trace)), s.tower = t.restrictionS.F.obj (SpTowerClasses.coefficient (ProjectiveLine Y) (SpTowerClasses.Arings l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) (ProjectiveLine Y))) ∧ s.limitFunctor = t.LS.R

proof.text: Apply full faithfulness of the degree-zero single functor to write the completed integral as the image of a unique completed-coefficient sheaf endomorphism φ. Naturality of the exact scalar-restriction/single comparison transports the finite integral projection identity to U(φ) followed by the ordinary coefficient projection.

For each site object and section x, apply coefficient_projection to φ(x) and x. The transported equality and coefficientForget give equality after each actual projection of the completed ring sheaf. Evaluate its inverse-limit cone in commutative rings; Concrete.isLimit_ext proves φ(x)=x. Thus φ is the identity, hence so is the derived integral.

Take the identity endomorphism of the required coefficient tower in degree zero. Its comparison with the completed unit is asIso(unitMap) followed by LS.R.mapIso of the exact restriction/single comparison. Result.unit_limit makes this invertible. Functor.map_id supplies the evaluations, and the proved integral identity supplies the square. Both required data equalities are reflexivity.
